notes: Read in full. Article dated 14 Oct; announcement on the Tuesday (13 Oct).
headline: Deezer says it is building a switch that will let listeners hide AI-generated music from its search results, due before the end of the year.
score_reason: Consumer feature that continues the AI-music labelling trend; announced 13 Oct, no change from pool score.
importance_line: Deezer listeners and human artists are affected; the feature is still being built and its accuracy depends on Deezer's AI detection, which is not independently tested here.
summary: TechCrunch reports that streaming service Deezer is working on a toggle that removes AI-generated tracks, albums and related artists from search results, expected before the end of the year, with chief executive Alexis Lanternier citing user demand. Deezer said in July that more than half of its daily uploads, about 90,000 tracks a day, were AI-generated, and it also cited a survey in which around 45% of its customers wanted a way to remove AI music.
